(NYSE: C) OCTOBER 13, 2026 ​ THIRD QUARTER 2026 RESULTS AND KEY METRICS ​ ​ CHAIR AND CEO COMMENTARY ​ ​ Citi Chair and CEO Jane Fraser said, “Our performance in the quarter, which included the best third-quarter revenue in a decade, positive operating leverage and meaningful improvement in our returns, reflects the continued disciplined and consistent execution of our strategy. “Services delivered another standout quarter, up 15%, with momentum in every driver. Equities rose 14% on strong performance in Asia and Prime, while FX and Spread Products drove overall growth of 6% in Markets. Banking also grew 6%, with particular strength in ECM, where we participated in the quarter's six largest transactions. Wealth saw steady, broad-based growth across all three businesses, with a return of over 14% — well above last year. In U.S. Consumer Cards, we had solid momentum in General Purpose cards, which drove loan growth and a return that exceeded 21%. “We returned over $4 billion to common shareholders while continuing to invest in growth and prepare for an AI-driven future. We expect to exceed this year's return target, even as we pull forward investments toward our 11-13% near-term goal —the next waypoints on our path to sustainable returns of 14-15%,” Ms. Fraser concluded. EPS UP 53% AS REPORTED; UP 27% EX-NOTABLE ITEM (3) RETURNED $4.1 BILLION IN THE FORM OF COMMON SHARE REPURCHASES AND COMMON DIVIDENDS PAYOUT RATIO OF 85% (4) COMMON EQUITY TIER 1 CAPITAL RATIO OF 12.8% (5) BOOK VALUE PER SHARE OF $115.61 TANGIBLE BOOK VALUE PER SHARE OF $101.59 (6) ​ ​ New York, October 13, 2026 – Citigroup Inc. today reported net income for the third quarter 2026 of $5.2 billion, or $2.85 per diluted share, on revenues of $23.8 billion. This compares to net income of $3.8 billion, or $1.86 per diluted share, on revenues of $22.1 billion for the third quarter 2025. ​ As previously disclosed (3) , third quarter results in the prior-year period included a notable item consisting of a goodwill impairment of $726 million ($714 million after-tax), recorded in operating expenses, related to Citi’s agreement to sell a 25% equity stake in Grupo Financiero Banamex, S.A. de C.V. (Banamex). ​ Revenues increased 8% from the prior-year period, driven by growth in Services, Wealth, Markets and Banking , partially offset by a decline in All Other. ​ Net income was $5.2 billion, compared to $3.8 billion in the prior-year period on a reported basis, driven by higher revenues and lower expenses, partially offset by a higher provision for credit losses. Excluding the notable item, net income in the prior-year period was $4.5 billion (3) . ​ Earnings per share of $2.85 increased from $1.86 per diluted share in the prior-year period on a reported basis, reflecting higher net income and a lower share count due to share repurchases. Net interest income increased 14%, driven by growth in Markets, Services, Wealth and U.S. Consumer Cards (USCC), partially offset by declines in All Other and Banking . Non-interest revenue decreased 4%, driven by declines in Markets and USCC , largely offset by growth in All Other, Services, Banking and Wealth . ​ Citigroup operating expenses of $14.0 billion were down 2% on a reported basis, driven by the absence of the notable item as well as lower professional services expenses, partially offset by higher transactional and product servicing expenses, deposit insurance costs, compensation and benefits as well as the contribution to the Citi Foundation. Excluding the notable item in the prior-year period, expenses were up 3% (3) . ​ Citigroup provision for credit losses was $2.6 billion, reflecting $2.2 billion of net credit losses and a net reserve build of $369 million, driven by changes in the macroeconomic outlook and portfolio growth. Net credit losses were unchanged from the prior-year period. The provision in the prior-year period was $2.5 billion, reflecting $2.2 billion of net credit losses and a net reserve build of $236 million, driven by portfolio growth and transfer risk, partially offset by changes in the macroeconomic outlook. ​ Citigroup net income was $5.2 billion in the third quarter 2026, compared to net income of $3.8 billion in the prior-year period on a reported basis, driven by higher revenues and lower expenses, partially offset by a higher provision for credit losses. Excluding the notable item, net income in the prior-year period was $4.5 billion (3) . Citigroup’s effective tax rate was approximately 26% in the third quarter 2026 compared to 29% in the third quarter 2025. ​ 2 ​ Citigroup’s total allowance for credit losses was $22.4 billion at quarter end, compared to $23.8 billion at the end of the prior-year period. Total ACL on loans was $20.1 billion at quarter end, compared to $19.2 billion at the end of the prior-year period, with a reserve-to-funded loan ratio of 2.5%, down from 2.7% in the prior-year period. Total non-accrual loans decreased $0.4 billion, or 12%, from the prior-year period to $3.3 billion. Corporate non-accrual loans decreased $0.3 billion, or 16%, from the prior-year period to $1.7 billion, driven by upgrades and repayments in Markets , partially offset by idiosyncratic downgrades in Services . Consumer non-accrual loans decreased $0.1 billion, or 5%, from the prior-year period to $1.5 billion, driven by Wealth , partially offset by Legacy Franchises, in All Other . ​ Citigroup ’ s end-of-period loans were $820 billion at quarter end, up 12% versus the prior-year period, driven by growth in Markets, USCC, Wealth, Banking and Services . Citigroup ’ s average loans were $809 billion in the third quarter 2026, up 12% versus the prior-year period, primarily driven by growth in Markets, Services, USCC and Wealth. ​ Citigroup ’ s end-of-period deposits were approximately $1.5 trillion at quarter end, up 9% versus the prior-year period, driven by growth in Service s. Citigroup ’ s average deposits were approximately $1.5 trillion in the third quarter 2026, up 11% versus the prior-year period, driven by growth in Services . ​ Citigroup ’ s book value per share of $115.61 at quarter end increased 7% versus the prior-year period, and tangible book value per share of $101.59 (6) at quarter end increased 6% versus the prior-year period. During the quarter, Citigroup returned $4.1 billion to common shareholders in the form of share repurchases and dividends. ​ Citigroup ’ s preliminary CET1 Capital ratio (5) was 12.8% at quarter end, unchanged from the end of the prior quarter, driven by net income and lower deduction from DTA and other, offset by common share repurchases, the payment of common and preferred dividends and unrealized losses on AFS securities. ​ Citigroup ’ s Supplementary Leverage ratio (5) for the third quarter 2026 was 5.0%, versus 5.2% at the end of the prior quarter. ​ 3 ​ ​ Services ($ in millions, except as otherwise noted) ​ ​ ​ 3Q’26 ​ ​ ​ 2Q’26 ​ ​ ​ 3Q’25 ​ ​ ​ QoQ% ​ ​ ​ YoY% Net interest income ​ ​ 3,671 ​ ​ 3,541 ​ ​ 3,121 ​ 4% ​ 18% Non-interest revenue ​ ​ 1,231 ​ ​ 1,198 ​ ​ 1,099 ​ 3% ​ 12% Treasury and Trade Solutions ​ ​ 4,902 ​ ​ 4,739 ​ ​ 4,220 ​ 3% ​ 16% Net interest income ​ ​ 801 ​ ​ 750 ​ ​ 702 ​ 7% ​ 14% Non-interest revenue ​ ​ 911 ​ ​ 893 ​ ​ 808 ​ 2% ​ 13% Securities Services ​ ​ 1,712 ​ ​ 1,643 ​ ​ 1,510 ​ 4% ​ 13% Total Services revenues ​ 6,614 ​ 6,382 ​ 5,730 ​ 4% ​ 15% ​ ​ ​ ​ ​ ​ ​ ​ ​ ​ ​ ​ ​ ​ Total operating expenses ​ ​ 2,976 ​ ​ 2,803 ​ ​ 2,707 ​ 6% ​ 10% ​ ​ ​ ​ ​ ​ ​ ​ ​ ​ ​ ​ ​ ​ Net credit losses ​ ​ 3 ​ ​ 5 ​ ​ 11 ​ (40)% ​ (73)% Net ACL build / (release) (a) ​ ​ (12) ​ ​ 46 ​ ​ (12) ​ NM ​ - reference.summary: Citigroup Inc., a diversified financial service holding company, provides various financial products and services to consumers, corporations, governments, and institutions. It operates through five segments: Services, Markets, Banking, U.S. Personal Banking, and Wealth. The Services segment includes treasury and trade solutions, which provides cash management, trade, and working capital solutions to multinational corporations, financial institutions, and public sector organizations; and securities services, such as cross-border support for clients, local market expertise, post-trade technologies, data solutions, and various securities services solutions.
